cv-writing.title: CV Writing Excellence
cv-writing.description: Master the art of creating compelling CVs that capture attention and secure interviews

layouts.title: Choose Your Layout
layouts.description: The structure you choose tells your career story. Each format serves different purposes and career stages.

chronological.title: Chronological CV
chronological.description: Best for candidates with steady career progression and no major gaps
chronological.when_to_use: When you have consistent work history in the same field

functional.title: Functional CV
functional.description: Focuses on skills rather than chronological work history
functional.when_to_use: When changing careers, returning to work, or have employment gaps

hybrid.title: Hybrid (Combination) CV
hybrid.description: Combines skills focus with chronological experience
hybrid.when_to_use: When you want to highlight both skills and steady progression
cons: May seem cluttered if not well-designed

essential_sections.title: Essential Sections
essential_sections.description: Every professional CV needs these fundamental sections, carefully crafted to tell your story.

professional_summary.title: Professional Summary
professional_summary.purpose: Your elevator pitch - capture attention in 3-4 sentences
professional_summary.structure: Start with your role/expertise, highlight key achievements, mention years of experience, end with value proposition
professional_summary.tone: Confident but not boastful, specific rather than generic

experience.title: Professional Experience
experience.placement: Usually after summary, but can come after skills for functional CVs
experience.format: Job title, Company name, Location, Dates (Month/Year format)
experience.description_structure: 2-4 bullet points per role, focusing on achievements not just duties
experience.achievement_formula: Action verb + What you did + Result/Impact + Numbers when possible

education.title: Education
education.placement: After experience (unless recent graduate, then place earlier)
education.include: Degree type, Institution, Graduation year, Relevant honours/achievements
education.note: Include GPA only if above 3.5 and you're within 2 years of graduation

skills.title: Skills
skills.placement: Can be prominent section or sidebar
skills.formatting: Use columns or categories, avoid rating systems unless you can back them up

bullet_points.title: Crafting Strong Bullet Points
bullet_points.description: Transform mundane job duties into compelling achievements that demonstrate your value.

examples.strong: Increased social media engagement by 150% across 5 platforms by implementing content calendar and user-generated campaigns, resulting in 2,000 new followers monthly

tailoring.title: Tailoring to Job Descriptions
tailoring.description: Your CV should feel like it was written specifically for each role, not as a generic document sent to hundreds of employers.

process.step1: Analyse the job description for keywords, required skills, and preferred experience
process.step2: Identify which of your experiences best match these requirements
process.step3: Reorder and rewrite sections to prioritise the most relevant information
process.step4: Mirror the language used in the job posting (without copying verbatim)
process.step5: Quantify achievements that relate to the role's key performance areas

keyword_strategy.identification: Look for repeated terms, required qualifications, and skills mentioned multiple times
keyword_strategy.integration: Naturally incorporate these terms into your experience descriptions and skills section
keyword_strategy.balance: Don't stuff keywords - maintain readability and authenticity
keyword_strategy.context: Use keywords within meaningful sentences that demonstrate your experience

common_mistakes.title: Mistakes That Kill Your Chances
common_mistakes.description: Avoid these common pitfalls that immediately signal amateur hour to recruiters and hiring managers.

content_mistakes.generic_objectives: 'Seeking a challenging position' tells employers nothing about your value
content_mistakes.duty_descriptions: Listing job duties instead of achievements makes you sound like everyone else
content_mistakes.irrelevant_information: Including every job since age 16 or personal hobbies unrelated to the role
content_mistakes.weak_language: Using passive voice and weak verbs like 'responsible for' or 'involved in'
content_mistakes.unexplained_gaps: Leaving employment gaps without brief, positive explanations

formatting_mistakes.inconsistent_formatting: Mixed fonts, varying bullet styles, or inconsistent date formats
formatting_mistakes.poor_spacing: Cramped text or excessive white space that makes reading difficult
formatting_mistakes.unprofessional_email: Using emails like partygirl@email.com instead of firstname.lastname@email.com
formatting_mistakes.outdated_design: Using templates that look like they're from 2010
formatting_mistakes.length_issues: Going over two pages without executive-level experience, or cramming everything onto one page

technical_mistakes.spelling_errors: Even one typo can eliminate you from consideration
technical_mistakes.grammar_issues: Poor grammar suggests lack of attention to detail
technical_mistakes.file_problems: Sending in formats that can't be opened or have corrupted formatting
technical_mistakes.contact_errors: Phone numbers or email addresses that don't work

understanding_ats.title: How ATS Systems Work
understanding_ats.description: Applicant Tracking Systems are the digital gatekeepers between you and human recruiters. Understanding how they parse and rank CVs is crucial for getting past this first hurdle.
understanding_ats.parsing_process: ATS software scans your CV to extract information into database fields, looking for keywords, dates, and standard formatting

formatting_for_ats.title: ATS-Friendly Formatting
formatting_for_ats.description: Simple, clean formatting ensures your CV is properly parsed and your information reaches human eyes.

do_use.formats: Standard bullet points, clear section breaks, consistent date formatting (MM/YYYY)
do_use.file_types: Word document (.docx) or PDF (if specified in job posting)

avoid.graphics: Images, charts, graphs, or logos that ATS cannot read
avoid.tables: Complex tables that may scramble your information
avoid.headers_footers: Important information in headers/footers may be ignored
avoid.columns: Multi-column layouts can confuse parsing algorithms
avoid.special_characters: Fancy symbols or non-standard bullet points

keyword_optimization.title: Strategic Keyword Integration
keyword_optimization.description: Keywords are the bridge between your experience and the ATS algorithm. Use them strategically, not desperately.

identification_process.job_description_analysis: Read through the posting 3-4 times, highlighting repeated terms and phrases
identification_process.skills_matching: Match your actual skills and experience with the keywords found
identification_process.industry_research: Look at similar roles to identify common terminology in your field
identification_process.competitor_analysis: Review profiles of people in similar roles on LinkedIn

integration_strategies.natural_inclusion: Weave keywords into your experience descriptions where they genuinely apply
integration_strategies.skills_section: List relevant technical skills and software mentioned in the job posting
integration_strategies.context_matters: Don't just list keywords - use them in meaningful sentences that demonstrate experience
integration_strategies.synonym_usage: Include variations of key terms (e.g., 'digital marketing' and 'online marketing')

testing_your_cv.keyword_density: Aim for natural keyword inclusion - not stuffing
testing_your_cv.readability_check: Your CV should read naturally to humans after keyword optimization
testing_your_cv.ats_simulators: Use free online ATS scanners to test how well your CV is parsed
testing_your_cv.feedback_loop: Continuously refine based on application response rates

cover-letters.title: Cover Letter Mastery
cover-letters.description: Transform your cover letter from generic afterthought to compelling narrative that complements your CV

opening.title: Compelling Openings
opening.description: Your opening paragraph determines whether the reader continues. Make it count by showing genuine interest and immediate value.

effective_approaches.connection: Mention a mutual connection or referral from someone in the company
effective_approaches.achievement: Lead with a quantified achievement that relates to the role
effective_approaches.company_knowledge: Reference recent company news, achievements, or initiatives that excite you
effective_approaches.value_proposition: Immediately state what unique value you bring to the role

examples.achievement_opening: Having increased digital engagement by 300% for my current employer's B2B campaigns, I'm excited to bring this growth-focused approach to [Company]'s expanding digital marketing team.
examples.connection_opening: Sarah Johnson mentioned that your team is looking for a data analyst who can bridge technical insights with business strategy—exactly the combination I've developed over five years in fintech.

body_paragraphs.title: Body Paragraph Excellence
body_paragraphs.description: Use 1-2 body paragraphs to tell a story that connects your experience to their needs. This isn't CV repetition—it's strategic storytelling.

paragraph_one.focus: Your most relevant experience and key achievements
paragraph_one.connection: Explicitly link your experience to requirements mentioned in the job posting

paragraph_two.focus: Why this company and role specifically excites you
paragraph_two.research: Demonstrate knowledge of company values, recent developments, or industry challenges
paragraph_two.alignment: Show how your career goals align with the company's direction
paragraph_two.culture_fit: Subtly indicate your compatibility with company culture

closing.title: Strong Closings
closing.description: End with confidence and a clear call to action. Show enthusiasm while maintaining professionalism.
effective_closings: I'd welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in [specific area] can contribute to [specific company goal/project]. I'll follow up next week to see when we might connect.
I'm excited about the possibility of bringing my [specific skills] to help [Company] achieve [specific goal mentioned in research]. Thank you for your consideration.
avoid: 'I look forward to hearing from you'
'Please let me know if you need anything else'

research_process.title: Company Research Framework
research_process.description: Superficial research shows. Deep research impresses. Here's how to go beyond the company website.

sources.company_website: Mission, values, recent news, leadership team, product/service evolution
sources.linkedin: Employee profiles, company updates, shared content, mutual connections
sources.industry_news: Recent mentions in trade publications, awards, partnerships, challenges
sources.glassdoor: Company culture insights, interview experiences, employee perspectives
sources.competitors: Market positioning, unique differentiators, industry trends

information_to_find: Industry challenges the company is addressing
Recent hiring patterns or team expansions

addressing_specifics.title: Addressing Specific Requirements
addressing_specifics.description: Generic cover letters are dead. Address their specific needs with your specific solutions.

requirement_matching.identify_key_requirements: Pull out 3-5 most important requirements from the job description
requirement_matching.evidence_gathering: Find specific examples from your experience that demonstrate each requirement
requirement_matching.story_crafting: Create mini-stories that show how you've successfully handled similar challenges
requirement_matching.impact_quantification: Include metrics and outcomes wherever possible

addressing_concerns.career_gaps: Brief, positive explanation focusing on skills maintained or developed
addressing_concerns.career_changes: Emphasise transferable skills and genuine passion for the new direction
addressing_concerns.overqualification: Show long-term interest and explain what genuinely attracts you to the role
addressing_concerns.underqualification: Focus on learning agility, relevant experience, and enthusiasm to grow

finding_your_voice.title: Authentic Professional Voice
finding_your_voice.description: Your cover letter should sound like you—professional you, but still recognisably you. Avoid corporate speak while maintaining professionalism.

voice_characteristics.confident_not_arrogant: State your achievements clearly without overselling or underselling
voice_characteristics.enthusiastic_not_desperate: Show genuine interest without sounding like you need this job to survive
voice_characteristics.specific_not_generic: Use concrete examples rather than vague statements about being 'passionate' or 'results-driven'
voice_characteristics.conversational_not_casual: Write as if you're speaking to a respected colleague, not texting a friend

industry_adaptation.title: Adapting Tone by Industry
industry_adaptation.description: Different industries have different communication styles. Match yours to theirs while staying authentic.

conservative_industries.approach: More formal tone, emphasis on stability and reliability, conservative language choices
conservative_industries.avoid: Overly casual language, industry slang, unconventional formats

creative_industries.approach: Show personality, demonstrate creativity in your writing, use industry-relevant language
creative_industries.opportunities: Creative formatting (within reason), storytelling, showing thought leadership

technical_industries.approach: Focus on precision, include technical terms appropriately, emphasise problem-solving

linkedin-optimization.title: LinkedIn Optimization
linkedin-optimization.description: Transform your LinkedIn profile into a powerful career advancement tool that works even while you sleep

professional_photo.title: Professional Profile Photo
professional_photo.description: Your photo is your first impression. It should convey professionalism, approachability, and confidence.

technical_requirements.composition: Head and shoulders, facing camera, professional background

industry_considerations.corporate: Business attire, conservative styling, neutral background
industry_considerations.creative: Can show more personality while maintaining professionalism
industry_considerations.technical: Clean, professional look that suggests reliability and attention to detail

headline_optimization.title: Compelling Headlines
headline_optimization.description: Your headline is prime real estate—use all 220 characters to tell your professional story and include searchable keywords.

examples.strong: Digital Marketing Manager | B2B SaaS Growth Specialist | Driving 40% Revenue Growth Through Data-Driven Campaigns | MarTech Enthusiast

headline_types.achievement_focused: Senior Sales Director | Consistently Exceeding Targets by 150% | Enterprise B2B Solutions | Team Leadership Excellence
headline_types.skill_focused: Full-Stack Developer | React, Node.js, Python | Building Scalable Web Applications | Open Source Contributor
headline_types.value_focused: Operations Manager | Process Optimization Expert | Reducing Costs While Improving Quality | Lean Six Sigma Black Belt

headline_optimization.keyword_strategy: Include terms recruiters search for in your industry, role-specific skills, and industry buzzwords that are genuinely relevant

summary_section.title: Compelling Summary
summary_section.description: Your summary is your elevator pitch expanded. Use this space to tell your professional story, highlight achievements, and show personality.

structure.opening_hook: Start with a compelling statement about your expertise or a notable achievement
structure.experience_overview: Summarise your professional journey and key areas of expertise
structure.achievements: Highlight 2-3 major accomplishments with metrics when possible
structure.values_vision: Share what drives you professionally and your vision for your career
structure.call_to_action: Invite connection and mention how people can reach you

writing_tips.length: Use most of the 2,000 character limit
writing_tips.formatting: Use bullet points, emojis (sparingly), and line breaks for readability
writing_tips.voice: Write in first person, be conversational yet professional
writing_tips.keywords: Naturally include industry keywords and skills
writing_tips.updates: Refresh regularly to reflect career progress and new interests

role_descriptions.title: Engaging Role Descriptions
role_descriptions.description: Transform job duties into compelling achievement stories that demonstrate impact and value.

examples.before: Responsible for managing social media accounts and creating content.
examples.after: Transformed brand presence across 5 social platforms, growing organic reach by 300% and engagement by 150% through strategic content creation and community building. Led cross-functional collaboration with design and product teams to ensure brand consistency.

section_structure.overview: 2-3 sentence overview of the role and your key responsibilities
section_structure.achievements: 3-5 bullet points highlighting specific accomplishments with metrics
section_structure.skills_keywords: Natural integration of relevant keywords and technical skills
section_structure.growth_story: Show progression and learning throughout the role

quantifying_impact.title: Quantifying Your Impact
quantifying_impact.description: Numbers tell stories that words alone cannot. Every achievement becomes more compelling with quantification.
quantifying_impact.approximation_guidelines: If you don't have exact numbers, use reasonable estimates based on available data, but mark them as approximate

skills_endorsements.title: Strategic Skills & Endorsements
skills_endorsements.description: Your skills section is crucial for searchability, but endorsements add social proof to your expertise claims.

skills_strategy.top_skills: List your most relevant and strongest skills first—these appear prominently on your profile
skills_strategy.skill_variety: Include a mix of technical skills, software proficiency, and soft skills
skills_strategy.industry_alignment: Ensure skills align with your target roles and industry standards
skills_strategy.skill_maintenance: Regularly review and update skills as you develop new competencies

endorsement_tactics.mutual_endorsements: Endorse colleagues' skills, and many will reciprocate
endorsement_tactics.strategic_requests: Ask specific colleagues to endorse skills that matter most for your goals
endorsement_tactics.diverse_endorsers: Seek endorsements from various people: managers, peers, direct reports, clients
endorsement_tactics.quality_over_quantity: Endorsements from respected professionals in your field carry more weight

connection_strategy.title: Strategic Connection Building
connection_strategy.description: Quality connections matter more than quantity. Build a network that provides mutual value and genuine professional relationships.

target_connections.industry_leaders: Thought leaders and influential people in your field
target_connections.peers: Professionals at similar levels who can share insights and opportunities
target_connections.company_employees: People at companies you're interested in joining
target_connections.alumni: Colleagues from previous companies, universities, or programmes

connection_approach.personalised_messages: Always include a personalised note explaining why you want to connect
connection_approach.mutual_connections: Leverage mutual connections for warm introductions when appropriate
connection_approach.value_first: Think about what you can offer before asking for anything
connection_approach.follow_up: Engage with connections' content and maintain relationships over time

content_engagement.title: Content & Engagement Strategy
content_engagement.description: Active participation in LinkedIn's content ecosystem increases your visibility and establishes thought leadership.

content_types.original_posts: Share insights, experiences, and industry observations
content_types.article_writing: Long-form content that demonstrates deep expertise
content_types.content_sharing: Curate and comment on relevant industry content
content_types.video_content: Personal updates, industry insights, or behind-the-scenes content

engagement_tactics.commenting: Add thoughtful comments to others' posts to increase visibility
engagement_tactics.liking_sharing: Engage with content from your network to stay visible
engagement_tactics.hashtag_strategy: Use relevant hashtags to increase content discoverability
engagement_tactics.consistency: Regular activity is more valuable than sporadic bursts

thought_leadership.industry_insights: Share unique perspectives on industry trends and developments
thought_leadership.problem_solving: Discuss challenges you've solved and lessons learned
thought_leadership.career_advice: Share experiences and advice for others in your field
thought_leadership.company_culture: Highlight positive aspects of your work environment and team

networking-outreach.title: Networking & Outreach
networking-outreach.description: Build meaningful professional relationships and create opportunities through strategic networking

outreach_strategy.title: Strategic Cold Outreach
outreach_strategy.description: Cold outreach isn't about asking for jobs—it's about building relationships and gathering insights that can lead to opportunities.

preparation.research_targets: Identify specific people rather than sending generic messages to many
preparation.company_research: Understand the company, recent news, challenges, and opportunities
preparation.person_research: Review their LinkedIn profile, recent posts, shared interests, or mutual connections
preparation.timing_consideration: Consider industry cycles, company announcements, or seasonal factors

message_framework.subject_line: Clear, specific, and intriguing without being clickbait
message_framework.opening: Personal connection, mutual contact, or specific research-based observation
message_framework.value_proposition: What you bring or what unique perspective you offer
message_framework.specific_ask: Clear, reasonable request (usually informational interview or advice)
message_framework.easy_out: Make it easy for them to decline politely

email_templates.title: Effective Outreach Templates
email_templates.description: These templates provide structure while allowing for personalisation based on your research and specific situation.

informational_interview.subject: Quick question about [specific topic/industry trend]
informational_interview.template:
Hi [Name],

I came across your profile while researching [specific topic/company/industry area] and was impressed by your work in [specific area]. Your recent post about [specific topic] particularly resonated with my experience in [relevant area].

I'm currently exploring opportunities in [field/industry] and would value your perspective on [specific question/trend]. Would you be open to a brief 15-minute conversation over coffee or phone in the coming weeks?

I understand you're busy, so please don't feel obligated if the timing isn't right.

Best regards,
[Your name]

industry_insight.subject: Fellow [industry] professional - question about [specific topic]
industry_insight.template:
Hi [Name],

I noticed we share a background in [specific area] and I've been following your insights on [specific topic/trend]. Your experience with [specific project/company/initiative] is exactly the kind of work I'm passionate about.

I'm particularly interested in understanding [specific question about industry/role/challenge]. Given your experience at [company/role], I'd love to hear your thoughts.

Would you be willing to share your insights over a brief call? I'm happy to work around your schedule.

Thanks for considering,
[Your name]

company_specific.subject: Admiration for [Company]'s work in [specific area]
company_specific.template:
Hi [Name],

I've been following [Company]'s innovative work in [specific area], particularly [specific project/initiative/achievement]. As someone with experience in [related area], I'm impressed by [specific detail about their work].

I'm exploring opportunities where I can contribute to [specific type of work/mission], and [Company] seems to be at the forefront of this space. I'd love to learn more about your experience there and the team's approach to [specific challenge/opportunity].

Would you be open to a brief conversation about your experience? I'm happy to buy you coffee or chat by phone at your convenience.

Best,
[Your name]

follow_up_strategy.title: Follow-up Best Practices
follow_up_strategy.description: Most opportunities come from thoughtful follow-up, not initial outreach. Here's how to follow up professionally and effectively.

timing.first_follow_up: 1 week after initial message if no response
timing.final_follow_up: 1 month later with value-added content or update

follow_up_approaches.value_added: Share relevant article, insight, or resource that might interest them
follow_up_approaches.update_sharing: Provide update on your situation or career progress
follow_up_approaches.different_angle: Approach from a different perspective or with a different ask
follow_up_approaches.seasonal_timing: Reach out during natural transition times (new year, after holidays)

networking_mindset.title: The Right Networking Mindset
networking_mindset.description: Effective networking is about building genuine relationships, not collecting contacts or asking for favours.

mindset_shifts.give_first: Look for ways to help others before asking for help yourself
mindset_shifts.long_term_view: Build relationships over time rather than transactional interactions
mindset_shifts.mutual_benefit: Seek relationships where both parties can gain value
mindset_shifts.authentic_interest: Show genuine interest in others' work and challenges
mindset_shifts.consistency: Regular, low-key engagement is better than sporadic intense contact

value_you_can_offer: Industry insights from your unique perspective
Connections to people in your network
Skills or expertise in your area of strength
Feedback or perspective on their projects
Support during their job search or career transitions

maintenance_strategies.title: Relationship Maintenance
maintenance_strategies.description: The best networkers are those who maintain relationships consistently, not just when they need something.

regular_touchpoints.content_engagement: Like, comment on, and share their LinkedIn posts and articles
regular_touchpoints.congratulatory_messages: Reach out when they announce promotions, awards, or achievements
regular_touchpoints.industry_updates: Share relevant news, articles, or opportunities that might interest them
regular_touchpoints.periodic_check_ins: Quarterly or bi-annual messages just to stay in touch
regular_touchpoints.event_invitations: Invite them to relevant events, webinars, or networking opportunities

relationship_levels.acquaintances: Light social media engagement, occasional shares of their content
relationship_levels.strong_connections: Regular meaningful conversations, mutual support, collaboration opportunities
relationship_levels.mentors_advisors: Consistent updates on your progress, seeking guidance, expressing gratitude

preparation.title: Pre-Event Preparation
preparation.description: Success at networking events starts long before you arrive. Preparation separates effective networkers from time-wasters.

research_phase.attendee_list: Review speaker lists and attendee information if available
research_phase.company_presence: Identify companies and representatives you'd like to meet
research_phase.session_planning: Choose sessions based on learning goals and networking opportunities
research_phase.goal_setting: Set specific, achievable goals (e.g., 'meet 3 people in product management')

materials_preparation.business_cards: Bring physical cards and set up digital sharing options
materials_preparation.linkedin_optimization: Ensure your profile is updated and professional
materials_preparation.questions_prepared: Develop thoughtful questions about industry trends and challenges

event_strategies.title: During Event Networking
event_strategies.description: Make genuine connections by focusing on others' interests and finding ways to provide value.
conversation_starters: What brings you to this event?
What session are you most looking forward to?
How are you finding the conference so far?
What trends are you seeing in your industry?
What's the most interesting project you're working on?

networking_techniques.active_listening: Focus on understanding their challenges and interests
networking_techniques.value_identification: Look for ways you might help or connect them with resources
networking_techniques.follow_up_planning: Set clear expectations for post-event contact
networking_techniques.graceful_transitions: Know how to politely end conversations and move on
networking_techniques.group_dynamics: Join and contribute to group conversations naturally

follow_up_planning.note_taking: Jot down key details about each person immediately after meeting
follow_up_planning.connection_promises: Keep track of any commitments you make to follow up or connect people
follow_up_planning.priority_ranking: Identify your most promising connections for immediate follow-up

post_event.title: Post-Event Follow-up
post_event.description: The real networking happens after the event. Timely, thoughtful follow-up converts brief meetings into lasting relationships.
post_event.timing: Reach out within 24-48 hours while the connection is still fresh

follow_up_approach.personalised_message: Reference specific conversation points from your interaction
follow_up_approach.value_delivery: Include promised resources, connections, or information
follow_up_approach.next_steps: Suggest concrete next steps if there was mutual interest
follow_up_approach.no_pressure: Keep initial follow-up light and professional

long_term_engagement.calendar_reminders: Set reminders to follow up periodically with valuable connections
long_term_engagement.content_sharing: Share relevant articles or opportunities with your new network
long_term_engagement.event_updates: Let them know about other relevant events or opportunities
long_term_engagement.relationship_building: Look for ways to deepen the most promising relationships

interview-preparation.title: Interview Excellence
interview-preparation.description: Master the art of interviewing to confidently showcase your value and secure job offers

star_method.title: STAR Method Framework
star_method.description: The STAR method provides structure for answering behavioral questions in a way that clearly demonstrates your capabilities and achievements.

situation.description: Set the context for your story
situation.tips: Be specific about when and where this happened, include relevant background

task.description: Explain your role and what needed to be accomplished
task.tips: Focus on your responsibilities and the challenges you faced

action.description: Detail the specific actions you took
action.tips: This is the most important part - be specific about YOUR actions, not the team's

result.description: Share the outcomes and what you learned
result.tips: Quantify results when possible, include lessons learned and skills developed

example.question: Tell me about a time you had to deal with a difficult team member.
example.situation: In my role as project manager, I was leading a cross-functional team of 8 people on a critical product launch with a 6-week deadline.
example.task: One team member consistently missed deadlines and was unresponsive in meetings, putting our timeline at risk.
example.action: I scheduled a private one-on-one meeting to understand their perspective and discovered they were overwhelmed with competing priorities. I worked with their manager to reallocate some responsibilities and created a more structured check-in schedule.
example.result: The team member's performance improved significantly, we launched on time, and the product exceeded initial sales targets by 15%. I learned the importance of addressing performance issues early and with empathy.

common_questions.title: Common Behavioral Questions
common_questions.description: Prepare compelling stories for these frequently asked behavioral questions across all industries.
leadership_teamwork: Tell me about a time you led a team through a difficult situation.
Describe a situation where you had to work with a difficult colleague.
Give me an example of when you had to persuade someone to see your point of view.
Tell me about a time you had to give constructive feedback to someone.
problem_solving: Describe a complex problem you solved at work.
Tell me about a time you made a mistake and how you handled it.
Give me an example of when you had to think creatively to solve a problem.
Describe a situation where you had to make a decision with incomplete information.
achievement_growth: Tell me about your greatest professional achievement.
Describe a time you exceeded expectations.
Give me an example of when you learned something new quickly.
Tell me about a time you took initiative on a project.
conflict_pressure: Describe a time you disagreed with your manager's decision.
Tell me about a time you had to work under significant pressure.
Give me an example of when you had to manage competing priorities.
Describe a situation where you had to adapt to significant change.

story_preparation.title: Building Your Story Bank
story_preparation.description: Develop a collection of 8-10 versatile stories that can answer multiple types of behavioral questions.

story_selection.diversity: Choose stories from different roles, projects, and time periods
story_selection.relevance: Select experiences that demonstrate skills relevant to your target roles
story_selection.impact: Focus on situations where you made a significant contribution or learned valuable lessons
story_selection.variety: Include both successes and challenges you overcame

story_categories.leadership_example: A time you led a team or initiative successfully
story_categories.problem_solving: A complex challenge you solved creatively
story_categories.collaboration: Working effectively with difficult people or across departments
story_categories.innovation: Implementing a new process or idea
story_categories.failure_recovery: A setback you overcame and what you learned
story_categories.growth_learning: Rapidly acquiring new skills or knowledge

technical_formats.title: Common Technical Interview Formats
technical_formats.description: Technical interviews vary by role and industry. Understanding the format helps you prepare effectively.

coding_interviews.format: Live coding challenges, algorithm problems, or take-home assignments
coding_interviews.preparation: Practice on platforms like LeetCode, HackerRank, or Codility
coding_interviews.focus_areas: Data structures, algorithms, system design, coding best practices
coding_interviews.tips: Think out loud, ask clarifying questions, write clean code, test your solutions

case_studies.format: Real-world business problems to solve using your expertise
case_studies.preparation: Research common industry challenges and framework approaches
case_studies.focus_areas: Problem-solving process, analytical thinking, business acumen
case_studies.tips: Structure your approach, ask relevant questions, show your thinking process

presentations.format: Present solutions to given problems or your past work
presentations.preparation: Practice explaining complex topics simply, prepare visual aids
presentations.focus_areas: Communication skills, subject matter expertise, stakeholder management
presentations.tips: Know your audience, use storytelling, prepare for questions

portfolio_reviews.format: Walk through your past work and explain your decisions
portfolio_reviews.preparation: Curate your best work, prepare detailed explanations
portfolio_reviews.focus_areas: Technical depth, decision-making process, learning from experience

company_research.deeper_insights: Industry position, competitors, challenges, growth areas

managing_nerves.title: Nervousness Management Techniques
managing_nerves.description: Some nervousness is normal and can even help performance. The key is managing it effectively.

physical_techniques.breathing_exercises: Deep breathing to calm your nervous system
physical_techniques.power_posing: Stand in confident poses for 2 minutes before the interview
physical_techniques.progressive_relaxation: Tense and release muscle groups to reduce physical tension
physical_techniques.arrival_strategy: Arrive early and use waiting time for final mental preparation

mental_techniques.positive_visualisation: Imagine the interview going well and receiving positive feedback
mental_techniques.reframing_nerves: Interpret nervous energy as excitement and preparation
mental_techniques.focus_shifting: Concentrate on learning about the role and company rather than being judged
mental_techniques.perspective_keeping: Remember that interviews are conversations, not interrogations

practical_strategies.mock_interviews: Practice with friends, family, or career counselors
practical_strategies.recording_practice: Record yourself answering common questions to identify areas for improvement
practical_strategies.outfit_comfort: Wear something that makes you feel confident and professional
practical_strategies.success_reminders: Review your achievements and qualifications before the interview

questions_to_ask.title: Strategic Questions to Ask Interviewers
questions_to_ask.description: Thoughtful questions demonstrate genuine interest and help you evaluate if the role is right for you.
role_specific_questions: What does success look like in this role after 6 months?
What are the biggest challenges facing the team right now?
How does this role contribute to the company's strategic goals?
What opportunities are there for professional development?
team_culture_questions: How would you describe the team dynamic?
What do you enjoy most about working here?
How does the company support work-life balance?
What's the communication style like between departments?
growth_opportunity_questions: What are the typical career paths from this position?
How does the company support employee development?
Are there opportunities to take on additional responsibilities?
What new initiatives or projects is the team working on?
questions_to_avoid: Salary and benefits (save for later stages unless they bring it up)
Information easily found on the company website
Negative questions about company problems or challenges
Questions that suggest you haven't prepared

crisis_management.reputation_recovery: Strategies for rebuilding reputation after professional setbacks

planning_process.action_planning: Create specific steps and timelines for closing identified gaps

daily_structure.break_scheduling: Plan regular breaks to maintain energy and perspective

priority_management.high_value_activities: Focus on networking and targeted applications over mass applications

priority_management.energy_matching: Match high-energy times with most important activities

warning_signs.behavioral_changes: Procrastinating on applications, avoiding networking, declining self-care
warning_signs.physical_symptoms: Sleep disruption, appetite changes, fatigue, stress-related health issues
warning_signs.performance_decline: Declining quality in applications, interviews, or networking interactions

prevention_strategies.realistic_expectations: Set achievable daily and weekly goals rather than overwhelming yourself
prevention_strategies.diversified_approach: Balance different job search activities to avoid monotony
prevention_strategies.support_system: Maintain connections with friends, family, and other job seekers for encouragement
prevention_strategies.professional_help: Consider career counseling or coaching if you're struggling
prevention_strategies.celebration_milestones: Acknowledge progress and small wins, not just final outcomes

recovery_tactics.strategic_breaks: Take planned breaks from job searching to recharge
recovery_tactics.perspective_shifting: Focus on learning and growth rather than just outcomes
recovery_tactics.activity_variety: Include enjoyable, confidence-building activities in your routine
recovery_tactics.goal_adjustment: Modify goals and expectations if they're consistently causing stress

salary_negotiation.title: Salary Negotiation Fundamentals

preparation_phase.market_research: Research salary ranges using Glassdoor, PayScale, industry reports, and networking
preparation_phase.value_documentation: Prepare specific examples of your achievements and value you'll bring
preparation_phase.total_package: Consider base salary, benefits, stock options, professional development, and work flexibility
preparation_phase.negotiation_strategy: Plan your approach, including opening offers and acceptable ranges

negotiation_phrases.value_emphasis: Given my experience in X and proven track record of Y, I believe...

negotiation_phrases.counter_offers: I appreciate the offer. Based on market research, would you be able to consider...
